speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a three-day-old neonate presenting with seizures and lethargy; can you tell me if your mother had a fever or any infections during your pregnancy or delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: 1100-g (2-lb 7-oz) newborn, 31 weeks' gestation. The patient was born three days ago with a birth weight of 1100 g at 31 weeks' gestation. The antenatal period was complicated by chorioamnionitis. Apgar scores were 3 and 6 at 1 and 5 minutes, respectively. The patient has become increasingly lethargic over the past 18 hours and experienced a tonic seizure lasting for 25 seconds.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hypoxic-Ischemic Encephalopathy (HIE) secondary to perinatal asphyxia.

The clinical picture of a low-birth-weight infant born to a mother with chorioamnionitis, followed by poor Apgar scores and subsequent seizures and lethargy, strongly suggests hypoxic-ischemic injury. I will immediately request an EEG to evaluate for seizures and a CT head to assess for injury severity.

REQUEST TEST: EEG, CT_Head
